image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of an orangutan sitting on a rocky surface. The subject is holding a bundle of dried grass or straw near its mouth, appearing to eat or manipulate it. The background consists of blurred green vegetation and grey rock walls, suggesting a zoo enclosure or naturalistic habitat.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Broad flat face with prominent cheek pads in mature males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject has a relatively smooth face without the large, fleshy cheek pads (flanges) characteristic of dominant adult male orangutans. It appears to be a female or a sub-adult male.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dark brown eyes with forward-facing binocular vision.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible eye is dark, round, and clearly positioned for forward-facing vision. The gaze direction is consistent with binocular alignment.
The ear visible on the left side of the head is small and partially obscured by fur, consistent with orangutan anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large body with tall, substantial proportions when standing.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject is seated and cropped at the torso/shoulders. Standing height and full body proportions cannot be verified from this angle.
The fur texture is visibly long, coarse, and shaggy. The color is a distinct reddish-brown/orange, matching the species description perfectly.
The visible torso area appears broad and robust, consistent with the barrel-chested morphology of great apes, even in a seated position.
The lower body and rear are not visible in the frame, so the absence of a tail cannot be visually confirmed, though it is biologically expected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Extremely long arms with exceptionally broad wingspan adapted for brachiation.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The arms are folded or holding food; the full length and wingspan are not extended or visible for measurement.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long-fingered hands with opposable thumbs and big toes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hand holding the straw is visible. The fingers appear long and slender, and the grip suggests an opposable thumb structure typical of primates.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness and minor 'haloing' where the fine fur strands meet the out-of-focus background. Some individual hairs blend into the background rather than having crisp occlusion boundaries, typical of AI generation or heavy compression.

The interaction between the fingers and the straw is slightly ambiguous. Some straw strands seem to merge into the fur or skin of the hand without clear physical separation or shadowing, creating a slight 'melted' look in the grip area.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification (Pongo pygmaeus) and rule out look-alikes like chimpanzees or gorillas based on facial structure and fur color.
To verify the anatomical correctness of the visible arm, shoulder, and hand structure, ensuring no extra limbs or impossible joint angles.
To closely inspect the boundary between the hand and the held object for fusion artifacts or missing fingers.
To analyze the micro-texture of the fur for signs of smearing, repetition, or plastic-like sheen indicative of AI generation.

focus_areas: Facial feature accuracy (eyes, nose, mouth symmetry)
Hand anatomy and finger count during object manipulation
Fur texture consistency and edge definition against background
Lighting coherence on the face and body
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the hand holding the straw. AI models often struggle with complex finger-object interactions. Check if the straw logically passes over/under fingers or if it merges. Also, verify if the fur texture looks naturally varied or if it has a 'painted' repetitive pattern.
